name: Originate and negotiate supply contracts with large customers
summary: Large industrial and commercial customers in Alberta buy power under fixed-price, index-plus, contract-for-differences or renewable PPA deals to steady their costs or meet carbon goals, and the generator signs them to lock in part of its merchant output. Originators answer the customer's enquiry, structuring analysts price the customer's load shape against the forward curve, credit and middle office check the counterparty and risk limits, the trading director approves, and legal and the customer's counsel negotiate the contract. Deals take weeks to months, most enquiries are lost to competitors, and price refreshes at execution mean a deal can fall over at the last step.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with a commercial team of originators and structuring analysts selling fixed-price power, CfDs and wind-backed PPAs to industrial and commercial customers.
baseline.notes: Includes renewable offtake deals such as the 18-year 100 MW Pembina PPA and C&I marketing of remaining wind output described in the 2021 AIF.

trigger: A large customer sends an enquiry or request for proposal for power supply, a CfD or renewable energy.
end_state: The contract is signed, booked and handed to contract administration, or the opportunity is declined, refused credit or lost.

volume.seasonality: More enquiries in late summer and autumn when industrial customers set next year's energy budgets and run RFPs for January start dates.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate; consistent with about 45 active customer contracts turning over every two to three years at a win rate of about one in three.

systems.name: Energy trading and risk management system
Load, price, wind and inflow forecasting models
Document management and engineering drawings repository

steps.name: Receive and log the customer enquiry
steps.description: The originator reads the request for proposal or enquiry from the industrial or commercial customer, notes the sites, annual load, term, product wanted (fixed price, index plus, contract for differences or renewable power with attributes) and deadline, and logs it in the deal pipeline.

next.condition: first meeting by phone or video

evidence.note: Customer contracts and renewable PPAs with corporate buyers described in the AIF and the BRC-Canada handout; times estimated.

steps.name: Travel to the customer's site
steps.description: The originator drives or flies to the customer's plant or head office in Alberta for the first meeting, usually in Calgary, Edmonton, Fort Saskatchewan or the oil sands region, and returns the same or next day.

evidence.note: Share of in-person meetings and travel times estimated from Alberta geography.

steps.name: Complete the site safety orientation
steps.description: Before entering an industrial customer's plant the originator completes the host's visitor safety orientation, signs in and wears the required protective equipment, which can take most of an hour at large chemical or oil sands sites.

control.basis: Host site visitor orientation and PPE rules under the customer's safety management system and the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code

evidence.note: Common practice at large Alberta industrial sites; estimated.

steps.name: Qualify the opportunity with the customer
steps.description: The originator meets the customer's energy manager and procurement lead to understand the load shape, sites, budget and sustainability goals, competing suppliers and decision process, then decides with the trading director whether the deal is worth pricing.

next.condition: not pursued (too small, wrong product, poor fit)

evidence.note: Qualification rate estimated.

steps.name: Run the customer credit check
steps.description: The credit analyst reviews the customer's financial statements and ratings, sets or confirms an unsecured credit limit and decides whether a letter of credit or parent guarantee will be needed for the tenor and size proposed.

control.basis: Credit risk policy: counterparty credit limits approved before a deal is offered

next.condition: credit acceptable, with or without security

evidence.note: The AIF describes procedures and controls on counterparty credit risk before entering contracts and monitoring of credit limits; times estimated.

steps.name: Build the price for the customer's load
steps.description: The structuring analyst cleans the customer's hourly meter data, builds the load shape, prices it against the forward curve with shaping, volume and credit premiums, transmission and losses, and carbon or renewable attribute values, and drafts a margin summary.

error.defect_description: The load shape or a cost adder is wrong, so the price misstates margin.

evidence.note: Pricing method and effort estimated from common practice for shaped load deals.

steps.name: Middle office checks the price and risk impact
steps.description: A risk analyst checks the forward curve and adders used in the price, calculates the effect of the deal on the portfolio's position and value at risk, and confirms it stays within limits.

control.basis: Commodity risk management policy: independent middle-office review of new deal pricing and limit use

evidence.note: The AIF lists risk control activities for market and credit risk in Energy Marketing; independent pricing review is the author's description.

steps.name: Director approves the indicative price
steps.description: The director of Alberta portfolio and trading reviews the margin summary, risk sign-off and strategic fit, and approves the indicative price and terms within the delegation of authority or asks for a different structure.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for customer contracts by tenor and volume

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Send the indicative proposal
steps.description: The originator writes the proposal or term sheet with price, volume, term, product structure, credit support and validity period, and sends it to the customer by the RFP deadline.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Customer evaluates competing offers
steps.description: The customer compares offers from several retailers and generators, often with a consultant, takes the shortlist to its own management, and comes back to shortlist, ask for a new price or decline.

next.condition: lost to a competitor or no deal

evidence.note: Win rate and decision time estimated.

steps.name: Negotiate the term sheet
steps.description: The originator negotiates price refresh mechanics, volume tolerance bands, credit support, term and termination rights with the customer's procurement team, checking any change with the structuring analyst.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Draft the contract
steps.description: The originator prepares the contract from the company's standard electricity supply agreement or contract-for-differences template and fills in the commercial schedule, then sends the draft to legal for review.

error.defect_description: A commercial term in the schedule does not match the agreed term sheet.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Legal review of the draft
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews the draft for termination, change-in-law, credit support, limitation of liability and regulatory terms, marks up departures from the standard and returns comments to the originator.

control.basis: Contract approval policy: legal review of all customer contracts before signature

evidence.note: Legal queue and review time estimated.

steps.name: Customer's counsel marks up the contract
steps.description: The draft goes to the customer, whose legal and procurement staff return a markup with requested changes to liability, termination, credit and billing terms.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Negotiate the markup
steps.description: The originator and legal counsel go through the markup with the customer on calls, decide which changes to accept within policy and whether another legal turn is needed before the text is final.

evidence.note: Number of turns estimated (about 1.7 legal reviews per signed deal).

steps.name: Confirm credit support documents
steps.description: The credit analyst checks the final credit terms, reviews any letter of credit or guarantee wording against the template, and confirms the exposure fits the approved limit.

control.basis: Credit risk policy: collateral and guarantee terms approved by credit

evidence.note: Collateral above credit limits from the AIF; times estimated.

steps.name: Refresh the price for execution
steps.description: On the agreed execution day the structuring analyst reprices the deal on the current forward curve, sends the final price to the originator and arranges for the term desk to hedge the position once the contract is signed.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Director gives final approval
steps.description: The director approves the final price and contract within the delegation of authority, or forwards long-tenor or large deals to the executive vice-president for signature authority.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for customer contracts by tenor and volume

evidence.note: Share estimated.

steps.name: Executive approves a long-tenor deal
steps.description: The executive vice-president reviews the deal summary for long-tenor or large renewable offtake deals, such as multi-year PPAs, and approves signature.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: executive approval above director limits

evidence.note: Long-tenor deals such as the 18-year Garden Plain PPA appear in the AIF; approval route estimated.

steps.name: Customer signs the contract
steps.description: The executable contract with the refreshed price goes to the customer for signature within the price validity window; if prices moved or internal approval stalls, the customer can walk away.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Book the deal and hand over to contract administration
steps.description: The originator books the signed contract in the ETRM system so the position and risk reports update, files it in the contract repository, and sends the billing and delivery set-up details to the contract administrator.

error.defect_description: A volume or price field is booked wrongly in the ETRM system.

evidence.note: Estimated.

exceptions.name: Reprice requested
exceptions.description: The customer or the director asks for a different structure or a new price, sending the deal back to the structuring analyst.

exceptions.name: Several legal turns
exceptions.description: The customer's markup changes liability or credit terms enough to need another legal review and another round with the customer.

exceptions.name: Lost at execution
exceptions.description: Forward prices move between approval and signature and the customer declines the refreshed price.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from enquiry to signature or loss, all enquiries
benchmarks.population: Industrial and commercial supply and renewable offtake deals of an Alberta generator

evidence.note: Author's estimate: lost or declined enquiries close within one to two months, signed fixed-price supply deals take two to four months, and corporate renewable PPAs six months or more.

benchmarks.population: Garden Plain wind PPA with Pembina (100 MW)

pain_points.description: Most enquiries are lost after the full pricing and approval effort, because customers run multi-supplier RFPs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Legal turns with the customer's counsel take weeks each and the price must be refreshed at execution, so deals can fall over late.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: First-time corporate buyers of renewable PPAs need time to learn the structure and terms, which lengthens negotiation.

assumptions: The organisation file lists the reviewed contract from lgl-review-contracts as a trigger; here it returns within a case (step s13), so it carries share 0.
Credit, middle office, legal and executive roles take part although the process map lists only originators, structuring analysts and the director.
Travel and site safety orientation apply to the 40 percent of deals with an in-person first meeting; no other physical resources are used.
No surge is given; autumn RFP rounds are ordinary seasonality.
All times, branch shares and win rates are tier C estimates.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Energy Marketing negotiates contracts with customers for the output of the generation assets and trades power, gas and environmental products; about 50 percent of capacity contracted in 2022 and 2023 and uncontracted merchant positions regularly hedged; Dow contract extension with a 10-year initial term from January 1, 2020; 18-year 100 MW renewable PPA with Pembina for Garden Plain and the remaining 30 MW marketed to commercial and industrial customers; counterparty credit limits monitored and collateral required above credit limits.

sources.title: Buying renewable energy in Canada: how BRC-Canada membership can simplify and accelerate (updated July 19, 2021)
sources.supports: Corporate and institutional buyers in Canada buy off-site renewable energy directly from developers, commonly through virtual power purchase agreements; Alberta's deregulated market lets buyers contract directly with developers; first-time buyers face a learning curve on the procurement process and PPA terms.
